seams.label: SOURCE-BASED · UNVALIDATED (QA of the merge, not an accuracy assessment)
seams.method:
For every ordered product pair (hi = higher merge priority, lo) whose footprints overlap in a zone, on the grid of the
level matching the coarser of the two native postings:
  * the finer product is block-averaged to that posting (removes the resolution difference, leaves real disagreement);
  * the seam band = pixels of hi within FEATHER_PX level pixels of hi's own valid-data edge where lo also has data
    (exactly where the merge blends the two);
  * delta = hi - lo in the band (after any applied co-registration).
Reported per pair: N, signed median, median |delta|, p99 |delta|, max |delta|, and the extra slope the feather adds
(atan(p99 |delta| / (FEATHER_PX * pixel))). Plus the eq <-> polar overlap (55-60 deg), which compares the same
merged sources on two grids (a reprojection check), once both zones exist.

reasons: Citation rule (R2 task 3): a population may be added only from a size-frequency distribution whose paper, table and values were checked in this session. No paper text was opened and checked here (e.g. Neukum et al. 2001 production function coefficients, an equilibrium-density relation, NAC boulder counts, Diviner rock abundance of Bandfield et al. 2011 were not verified line by line), so none is used.

Double counting: the VISUAL amplitude is calibrated to LOLA LDRM_32_50, the 5-spot roughness measured on the real surface, which already contains the topographic variance of the small craters and boulders inside each 25 m shot pattern. Adding a crater field on top would push the displayed 5-spot roughness above LOLA (the hard test in tools/globe/tests/test_globe_roughness.py would catch it) unless the fractal noise were reduced by a published partition of roughness between craters and the background, which was not available.

Scale: the finest VISUAL post built is 5 m (roughness check) and the pre-built tiles are 10-20 m; most boulders (< 5 m) are below every VISUAL pixel, so a boulder population would not change the displayed surface.
Diviner rock abundance (Bandfield et al. 2011) is not on disk (S2 did not download it).
visual_population.what_would_enable_it: download Diviner RA (PDS), read and cite the SFD tables (paper, table, coefficients), add craters as a share of the LDRM variance budget (noise reduced accordingly), keep the LOLA-spread test green.
